narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, it judged failure four times more likely than success, and the school used that prediction as part of its admission decision.

The strongest driver was your third-year class standing. You were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged near the sixth decile; this signal pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other. The second strongest was your LSAT score of 19.30, well below the accepted-student average of 37.18; it also pushed toward failure. Third was your first-year class standing: first decile compared with an accepted average near 6.00, again pushing toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was close to the accepted average of 3.23 and was not among the top influences.

To improve future applications, focus on raising your LSAT through structured preparation and consider a retake, strengthen your academic record, and seek admissions advising. Ask schools to consider context for your early class standing, and apply where holistic review can weigh your improvement and readiness.
